stories.title: Sierra Doubles Valuation to $30B, ARR Passes $400M as Fortune 50 Adoption Accelerates
stories.body: Sierra raised $1.75 billion in a Series F led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed on November 23, 2026, nearly doubling its valuation from $15.8B in May to $30B, with annual recurring revenue topping $400M in October—just over two and a half years after launch. The company says it now serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, with clients including HSBC, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, and Walmart, and charges only when its agents deliver outcomes. Sierra simultaneously released Personal Agent Protocol (Poppy) v1.0, a new interoperability standard already live with Meta's Muse agent and enabled for every Shopify merchant.
stories.why: Sierra is the benchmark competitor your prospects will reference—its outcome-based pricing model and $30B valuation set the expectation ceiling on what enterprise CX AI is worth. Its protocol work with Meta and Walmart signals it is building the agent-to-agent layer that could route around retailer-specific context solutions unless Graas can demonstrate superior grounding in retail data.

stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Cresta for a Reported $2.7B to Add Voice AI to Agentforce
stories.body: Salesforce signed a definitive agreement on November 2, 2026 to acquire Cresta, a voice-first contact center AI platform used by Marriott, Comcast, and Alaska Airlines, in a deal reported by The Information at $2.7 billion. Cresta's platform combines autonomous voice agents, real-time human-rep coaching, and full interaction analysis on one stack; Salesforce says Cresta will continue to support existing third-party contact center and telephony platforms after close. The deal is Salesforce's third acquisition announcement in two weeks, following Braze and Rune Technologies, and closes in Salesforce's fiscal Q1 2028.
stories.why: Cresta is now off the market as an independent option, consolidating voice AI into the Salesforce/Agentforce orbit—any retail prospect running a non-Salesforce CRM stack faces a forced migration question at renewal. For Graas sellers, this shrinks the independent voice-agent landscape and raises urgency to position a knowledge-layer architecture that is CRM-agnostic before Agentforce lock-in hardens.

stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 32% of Enterprises Skipped a Software Buy to Build In-House, Yet Only 6% See Real EBIT Impact
stories.body: McKinsey's 'State of AI: On the Road to ROI,' published August 25, 2026, surveyed 1,719 leaders across 97 countries and found that 32% of organizations decided against buying at least one software product or feature because they could build it with agentic coding tools—rising to nearly half among AI high performers. Despite this, the share of organizations reporting any EBIT impact from AI remained flat at 37%, and only 6% qualified as high performers (those attributing 5%+ of EBIT to AI). Among large enterprises (revenue >$1B), 40% now report scaling AI agents in at least one function, up from 27% the prior year.
stories.why: The 32% build-vs-buy stat is the objection you will face on every enterprise call—prospects believe they can code their way to a retail agent. The 6% EBIT-impact reality is your counterpoint: building the agent is cheap; building the governed context layer that makes it accurate in retail workflows is not, and that is exactly what Graas provides.

stories.title: Gartner 2026 Playbook: 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge' — and 40% of Agentic Projects Will Be Cancelled by 2027
stories.body: Gartner's September 2026 research, 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge,' establishes the enterprise context graph as the foundational layer that moves agentic AI from pilot to production, arguing that agents need a shared, trusted context foundation to operate at enterprise scale. A separate Gartner prediction, published June 2025 and cited in a November 2, 2026 adoption analysis, forecasts that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by end of 2027, with a further prediction that 70% of enterprises will abandon agentic AI built by vendor forward-deployed engineering by 2028. Gartner also projects that 60% of large enterprises running AI agents in production will face external accountability requirements for autonomous actions by 2030, up from under 10% today.
stories.why: Gartner's context-graph framing is the analyst language your economic buyers are reading right now—use it to position Graas as the architecture that closes the gap between pilot and production. The 40% cancellation forecast is the stall-rate number that makes urgency concrete: pilots die not for lack of models but for lack of governed context, which is precisely the problem Graas solves.

stories.title: CPG Agentic AI in Production: Trade Deduction Agent Recovers $6.5M; McKinsey Finds 71% of CPG Firms Use AI but None Have Truly Scaled
stories.body: Tredence's agentic deduction-management solution, integrated across 30+ systems including SAP, EDI, and retailer portals, evaluated trade deductions automatically and recovered $6.5M from roughly $40M in addressable deduction spend for one unnamed enterprise CPG client. NVIDIA's 2026 State of AI in Retail and CPG survey found 51% of retail and CPG leaders already run AI agents in production—38% in supply chain and logistics—yet McKinsey separately found 71% of CPG companies use AI in at least one function but notes no CPG player has truly scaled it, citing the most common barrier as data quality rather than model capability. BCG's May 2026 supply chain report confirms agentic AI can eliminate the historic tradeoff between effectiveness and efficiency in replenishment, but warns that AI-related incidents rose 21% from 2024 to 2025.
stories.why: The $6.5M deduction-recovery outcome is proof-point currency for a sales call—it shows agents delivering against a measurable P&L line in a real CPG workflow. The McKinsey 'pilot purgatory' finding and NVIDIA's data-as-the-top-barrier stat explain why: without a governed context layer unifying SKU, retailer portals, and ERP data, agents cannot scale past the pilot, which is the exact entry point for Graas.
